chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about the man who fabricates (slanders) upon his wife. He said: He is whipped, then separation is made between them, and he does not perform Li'an with her until he says: 'I testify that I saw you doing such and such.'
ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for Li'an when a husband slanders his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural distinction between general slander (Ghazl) and the specific oath ritual of Li'an, emphasizing that mere accusation is insufficient to trigger the latter. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential requirement for the accuser to explicitly declare witnessing the act before the formal separation and cursing process can commence, ensuring legal precision in marital disputes.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who fabricated upon his wife. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be whipped, then there would be separation between the two, and he would not curse her until he is saying, ‘I testify that I saw you, such and such being done with you’.
